info.title: AWorld API - App Endpoints
info.description: The App context provides APIs for integrating with and extending applications built on the AWorld platform. These APIs are designed for use in end-user applications and client-side interfaces.

post.description:
Creates a new activity log entry for a user. 
    This endpoint is intended for backend systems to record custom user activities defined through the Dashboard. 
    Built-in activities such as quizzes, stories, and other internal events are automatically tracked and should not be manually created through this endpoint.

Only applicable when authenticating with M2M client credentials (OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant); ignored for regular user access tokens. When provided, the request acts on behalf of the user identified by this external ID. Most endpoints require one of x-user-id or x-external-user-id when using client credentials. Mutually exclusive with x-user-id.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid). Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it verbatim when retrying that same event.

Retries to this endpoint are not de-duplicated: every accepted request is recorded as a separate activity log, including one that repeats an earlier request exactly. Submit each event once.

For a once-per-event guarantee that does not depend on timing, send `activityLogId` instead: a reuse carrying different data is rejected with a 409 and writes nothing.

activityId.description: The unique ID of the activity. Should be a nanoid

outcome.description:
Whether the user succeeded at the activity, as reported by the caller.

It is kept as sent and never computed; leave it out for an activity with no success or failure. Mission, streak and reward rules can test it as event.outcome. The failure value is FAILURE, not the FAIL that quiz and learning path logs use.

value.description:
How much of the activity this log records, 1 when omitted.

It is kept as sent. Mission, streak and reward rules can read it as event.value, for example to advance a mission by the amount reported; a rule that does not read it counts every log alike, whatever its value.

activityLogId.description: Optional caller-supplied ID, stored verbatim; omit it for a generated one. Must be exactly 21 characters from the alphabet A-Za-z0-9_-, or the request is rejected with a 400. A deterministic value gives permanent once-per-content semantics, with no time limit: a reuse is rejected with a 409 and writes nothing, whether or not it carries the same data as the original. Derive it from the userId as well as the content — IDs need only be unique per user here, but must be unique per workspace downstream, so two users must never produce the same one. A base64url SHA-256 truncated to 21 characters fits.

completedAt.description:
When the activity was completed, as an ISO 8601 date-time. Optional: when omitted, the server records the time it processed the request.

A server-filled value is applied after the request has already been identified for de-duplication purposes, so omitting this field can never make two otherwise-identical submissions distinct — only a value you send yourself can. If you send it for that reason, use full time-of-day precision: a date-only or hour-truncated value repeats across submissions and leaves them identical.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Where the assignment is in its active window: PENDING before startsAt, ACTIVE from startsAt until endsAt, ENDED after endsAt. It is set from those two dates when the assignment is created and changes on its own as each one passes; an assignment without endsAt stays ACTIVE once started. The app offers only ACTIVE assignments and does not let the user start a PENDING or ENDED one, and only an ACTIVE assignment can be retried.

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: Whether the user can start the assigned item yet. LOCKED: the user cannot start it until it is unlocked, and the app does not offer it as something to do until then. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its target or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

parameters.name: x-idempotency-key
parameters.description:
Idempotency key for this request. Any string is accepted (for example a UUID or a nanoid).

The de-duplication key is always derived from the whole request: its validated body, path and query parameters, and declared headers. This header is one of those inputs — it is never the key on its own, and sending it does not change how the key is derived. It adds a value you control to the hash; omitting it leaves that value out.

Send a value that is unique per real-world event, and repeat it unchanged when retrying that event. Two things follow from the key covering everything. A retry is recognised as a duplicate only if it repeats this header AND the rest of the request identically — reuse the key with any other field changed and it is a new request, which is processed and written separately. Conversely, with no header at all the request content is the only identity available, so two genuinely distinct events that happen to carry identical content are indistinguishable and the second is treated as a retry of the first.

De-duplication covers the first hour after a request is accepted. An identical request sent after that window is processed as a new one.

A de-duplicated request is answered with the original response: HTTP 200 carrying the record the first request created, with its original identifier and timestamps. Nothing further is written and no error is returned. Neither the status code nor the response headers mark the response as a replay, so reconciling the returned identifier and timestamps against what was submitted is how a caller detects one.

assignmentRuleId.description: The ASSIGN rule that created this assignment (rules with duplicatePolicy ALLOW or DISALLOW_ACTIVE). Unset on MERGE-managed assignments, which carry contributingRuleIds instead.

contributingRuleIds.description: Present on MERGE-managed assignments only: the IDs of the ASSIGN rules (duplicatePolicy MERGE) whose desired state currently contributes to this assignment. The assignment reflects the union of these rules — it is unlocked if any of them wants it unlocked, required if any of them requires it, and revoked only when none of them desires the target anymore. Mutually exclusive with assignmentRuleId.

items.description: The unique ID of the assignment rule

groupId.description: Optional grouping label, copied from the rule that created the assignment or set by the caller on a manual one. Rules that form one pathway, such as an ASSIGN rule and the UNLOCK rules that open its items one after another, share a groupId. It has no effect on what the user sees or can start, and a later change to the rule's groupId is not applied to existing assignments. An assignment merged from several rules takes it from one of them.

periodId.description: Identifies the timeframe period and is computed by the platform, never sent by API callers. It is PERMANENT for a permanent timeframe and the start instant in UTC for a date range. For a recurring rule it is the current day (2026-09-24), ISO week (2026-W39) or month (2026-09) in the timezone the rule uses, and for a CUSTOM recurrence the time of the schedule's last run, in UTC.

timeframeType.description: How the assignment's active window is meant to be bounded: RANGE runs from startsAt to endsAt, PERMANENT has no endsAt and never ends. An assignment created by a recurring rule is RANGE and covers one period of the rule, which creates a new assignment for each period.

startsAt.description: When the assignment starts, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Until then the assignment is PENDING, from then on ACTIVE. A manual assignment takes the value sent, which may be in the past: the assignment is then created ACTIVE, or ENDED if endsAt has passed too. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: the moment the assignment is created for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeStartsAt for a RANGE rule, and the start of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it, and moving a RANGE rule's start creates a new assignment instead.

endsAt.description: When the assignment ends, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC; unset when it never ends. After it the assignment is ENDED. On a manual assignment, send it with timeframeType RANGE and leave it out with PERMANENT. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: none for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeEndsAt for a RANGE rule, and the end of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it.

state.description: Where the assignment is in its active window: PENDING before startsAt, ACTIVE from startsAt until endsAt, ENDED after endsAt. It is set from those two dates when the assignment is created and changes on its own as each one passes; an assignment without endsAt stays ACTIVE once started. The app offers only ACTIVE assignments and does not let the user start a PENDING or ENDED one, and only an ACTIVE assignment can be retried.

visibility.description: Whether the user can start the assigned item yet. LOCKED: the user cannot start it until it is unlocked, and the app does not offer it as something to do until then. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its target or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

assignmentType.description: Whether the assignment is compulsory or suggested for the user. REQUIRED marks a compulsory assignment and OPTIONAL a suggested one; the app shows survey assignments the same way whichever the type. An assignment created by a rule takes its type from the rule and follows later changes to it, except that a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while the user has another active or pending REQUIRED assignment for the same target.

priority.description: Ordering weight among the user's assignments: lower values come first. Within the same state, the assignment list shows unlocked assignments before locked ones and orders each group by priority; an UNLOCK rule that unlocks a limited number of assignments at a time also picks them in this order. An assignment created by a rule takes its priority from the rule's order and follows later changes to it; a manual assignment has the value sent when it was created, 0 when omitted.

unlockedAt.description: When the assignment was unlocked, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Set when an UNLOCK rule unlocks it or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED and on one created UNLOCKED.

unlockedByRuleId.description: The UNLOCK rule that unlocked the assignment. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED, on one created UNLOCKED, and when it was unlocked by an ASSIGN rule being evaluated again rather than by an UNLOCK rule.

currentAttempt.description: Which attempt at the assigned item the user is on, starting at 1. Each retry of the assignment adds one and starts a fresh attempt, with nothing carried over from the previous one; the progress returned with the assignment is, by default, that of the current attempt. A retry is accepted only while the assignment is ACTIVE and UNLOCKED, otherwise it fails with 409 Conflict.

contributingRuleIds.description: Present on MERGE-managed assignments only: the IDs of the ASSIGN rules (duplicatePolicy MERGE) whose desired state currently contributes to this assignment. The assignment reflects the union of these rules — it is unlocked if any of them wants it unlocked, required if any of them requires it, and revoked only when none of them desires the learning path anymore. Mutually exclusive with learningPathRuleId.

items.description: The unique ID of the learning path rule

groupId.description: Optional grouping label, copied from the rule that created the assignment or set by the caller on a manual one. Rules that form one pathway, such as an ASSIGN rule and the UNLOCK rules that open its learning paths one after another, share a groupId. It has no effect on what the user sees or can start, and a later change to the rule's groupId is not applied to existing assignments. An assignment merged from several rules takes it from one of them.

periodId.description: Identifies the timeframe period and is computed by the platform, never sent by API callers. It is PERMANENT for a permanent timeframe and the start instant in UTC for a date range. For a recurring rule it is the current day (2026-09-24), ISO week (2026-W39) or month (2026-09) in the timezone the rule uses, and for a CUSTOM recurrence the time of the schedule's last run, in UTC.

timeframeType.description: How the assignment's active window is meant to be bounded: RANGE runs from startsAt to endsAt, PERMANENT has no endsAt and never ends. An assignment created by a recurring rule is RANGE and covers one period of the rule, which creates a new assignment for each period.

startsAt.description: When the assignment starts, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Until then the assignment is PENDING, from then on ACTIVE. A manual assignment takes the value sent, which may be in the past: the assignment is then created ACTIVE, or ENDED if endsAt has passed too. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: the moment the assignment is created for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeStartsAt for a RANGE rule, and the start of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it, and moving a RANGE rule's start creates a new assignment instead.

endsAt.description: When the assignment ends, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC; unset when it never ends. After it the assignment is ENDED, and until then the app shows the user how many days are left on the learning path's page. On a manual assignment, send it with timeframeType RANGE and leave it out with PERMANENT. An assignment created by a rule takes it from the rule: none for a PERMANENT rule, the rule's timeframeEndsAt for a RANGE rule, and the end of the period it covers for a recurring rule. It is fixed at creation: a later change to the rule's dates is not applied to it.

state.description: Where the learning path assignment is in its active window: PENDING before startsAt, ACTIVE from startsAt until endsAt, ENDED after endsAt. It is set from those two dates when the assignment is created and changes on its own as each one passes; an assignment without endsAt stays ACTIVE once started. The app lists only ACTIVE learning path assignments, and only an ACTIVE one can be retried.

visibility.description: Whether the user can start the assigned learning path yet. LOCKED: the user sees the assigned learning path, marked as locked, but cannot start it until it is unlocked. UNLOCKED: the user can open and start it. A LOCKED assignment is unlocked by an UNLOCK rule for its learning path or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it to the user is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED; rules only ever unlock an existing assignment, never lock it again.

assignmentType.description: Whether the learning path is compulsory or suggested for the user. REQUIRED: shown in the app among the user's assigned (required) learning paths. OPTIONAL: shown in a separate suggested section, which the app hides when empty. Once started, a learning path is listed with the others whatever its type. An assignment created by a rule takes its type from the rule and follows later changes to it, except that a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while the user has another active or pending REQUIRED assignment for the same learning path.

priority.description: Ordering weight among the user's learning path assignments: lower values come first. Within the same state, the assignment list shows unlocked learning paths before locked ones and orders each group by priority; an UNLOCK rule that unlocks a limited number of learning paths at a time also picks them in this order. An assignment created by a rule takes its priority from the rule's order and follows later changes to it; a manual assignment has the value sent when it was created, 0 when omitted.

unlockedAt.description: When the assignment was unlocked, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Set when an UNLOCK rule unlocks it or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED and on one created UNLOCKED.

unlockedByRuleId.description: The UNLOCK rule that unlocked the assignment. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED, on one created UNLOCKED, and when it was unlocked by an ASSIGN rule being evaluated again rather than by an UNLOCK rule.

currentAttempt.description: Which attempt at the learning path the user is on, starting at 1. The user can retry while the assignment is ACTIVE and the current attempt is complete with outcome PASS or FAIL; a retry adds one and starts the next attempt, and a retry in any other situation fails with 409 Conflict. After FAIL the new attempt starts from scratch; after PASS it keeps what the user already did, except quizzes whose outcome was not SUCCESS, which have to be taken again. The progress returned with the assignment is, by default, that of the current attempt.

- contain: the whole image is shown inside the screen, without cropping.

- center: the image is centered on the screen.
- top, bottom, left, right: the image is aligned to that edge of the screen and centered along it.

With cover it decides which part of the image stays in view when the rest is cropped. It has an effect only when a background image is shown. The link does not add the item to the parent's items, which are edited on the parent. timeframeType.description:
Sets how long this leaderboard instance stays open and whether the series continues after it closes.

- PERMANENT: the instance never closes and nothing follows it; timeframeEndsAt must not be set.
- RANGE: the instance runs once, from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, both required.
- RECURRING: the instance runs from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, both required, and once it ends a new instance for the next period opens automatically, per recurrence.

Can be changed after creation: switching away from RECURRING drops recurrence, and switching to PERMANENT drops timeframeEndsAt.

timeframeTimezoneType.description:
Chooses how this instance's active window relates to users in different timezones.

- FIXED: the window runs exactly from timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, and timeframeTimezone, which is required, is also the zone RECURRING periods roll over in.
- USER: timeframeTimezone is not used; the instance's state follows timeframeStartsAt and timeframeEndsAt as absolute times, and RECURRING periods roll over in UTC.

The scored window itself, timeframeStartsAt to timeframeEndsAt, is the same absolute time for every user either way.

recurrence.description:
Sets how a RECURRING leaderboard starts its next period once the current one ends.

- DAILY: every calendar day.
- WEEKLY: every week, Monday to Monday.
- MONTHLY: every calendar month.
- CUSTOM: repeats the exact length of the instance's own first period, one period after another, with no calendar alignment.

Boundaries are computed in the timezone timeframeTimezoneType selects, UTC when it is USER. Required when timeframeType is RECURRING and rejected otherwise.

cadence.description:
Sets how often the user must act to keep the streak alive.

- DAY: the user must contribute a matching event every calendar day.
- WEEK: the user must contribute at least once every ISO calendar week.

Missing a required day or week breaks the streak, unless freezeEnabled lets the user spend virtual currency to keep it going. DAY cadence only accepts DAYS as the metric.

metric.description:

- DAYS: one active day.
- WEEKS: one active week.

Must be DAYS when cadence is DAY, which create checks. Fixed when the rule is created; update cannot change it.

matchType.description:

- INSTANCE: matches one specific item, named by matchEntityId.
- ENTITY: matches every item of matchEntity's type.
- TAG: matches every item of matchEntity's type carrying the tag named by matchEntityId.

matchEntityId is required with INSTANCE and TAG, which create checks, and unused with ENTITY. matchCondition can narrow the match further.

assignmentType.description: Whether the learning path is compulsory or suggested for the user. REQUIRED: shown in the app among the user's assigned (required) learning paths. OPTIONAL: shown in a separate suggested section, which the app hides when empty. Once started, a learning path is listed with the others whatever its type. An assignment created by a rule takes its type from the rule and follows later changes to it, except that a change to OPTIONAL is not applied while the user has another active or pending REQUIRED assignment for the same learning path.

priority.description: Ordering weight among the user's learning path assignments: lower values come first. Within the same state, the assignment list shows unlocked learning paths before locked ones and orders each group by priority; an UNLOCK rule that unlocks a limited number of learning paths at a time also picks them in this order. An assignment created by a rule takes its priority from the rule's order and follows later changes to it; a manual assignment has the value sent when it was created, 0 when omitted.

unlockedAt.description: When the assignment was unlocked, as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. Set when an UNLOCK rule unlocks it or when an ASSIGN rule that assigns it is evaluated again and now gives it UNLOCKED. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED and on one created UNLOCKED.

unlockedByRuleId.description: The UNLOCK rule that unlocked the assignment. Unset while the assignment is LOCKED, on one created UNLOCKED, and when it was unlocked by an ASSIGN rule being evaluated again rather than by an UNLOCK rule.

currentAttempt.description: Which attempt at the learning path the user is on, starting at 1. The user can retry while the assignment is ACTIVE and the current attempt is complete with outcome PASS or FAIL; a retry adds one and starts the next attempt, and a retry in any other situation fails with 409 Conflict. After FAIL the new attempt starts from scratch; after PASS it keeps what the user already did, except quizzes whose outcome was not SUCCESS, which have to be taken again. The progress returned with the assignment is, by default, that of the current attempt.

externalId.description: Your own identifier for the person, for matching them with your systems; GET /users/by-external-id/{externalId} finds the user by it. Creating a user with an externalId that another user of the workspace already has is rejected with 409 Conflict.

nickname.description: The name the person goes by in the app, shown there in place of their first and last name. It must be unique within the workspace: a nickname another user already has is rejected with 409 Conflict. The app asks a person who has none to choose one when they sign in, and notification emails greet the person by it.

currency.description: The person's own choice of currency for money amounts, as an ISO 4217 code; unset when they have not made one.

role.description:
The person's role in the workspace, which decides what they may do and which apps they can sign in to.

- owner: everything an admin can do, and the only role that can give or remove the owner role, since a role can be assigned only at or below the assigner's own.
- admin: creates, edits, publishes and deletes content, manages users and changes the workspace settings.
- manager: creates, edits and publishes content, but cannot delete it, manage users, change the workspace settings or read analytics in the console.
- member: reads content and submits answers in the app, and cannot sign in to the console.
- viewer: reads everything, the console included, but submits nothing and changes only their own profile.

A caller can give only a role at or below their own, and only an admin or an owner can give viewer; machine credentials act as admin, so they cannot create an owner. Any other role is rejected with 403.

status.description:
Whether the person can use the workspace.

- active: the person can sign in, and takes one of the workspace's seats.
- suspended: the person cannot sign in and is told to contact their administrator; the app signs them out if it is open, and any other session ends when it next refreshes. Their record and history are kept, and their seat is given back.

Only admins and owners can change it. Reactivating a suspended user takes a seat again, and fails when the workspace has none free.

referredCount.description: How many people have joined the workspace through this user's referral. It starts at 0 and the platform adds one each time someone joins with the user's referral code or referral link; rule conditions on users can test it.
